items.title: As Holidays Approach, No One Cares About Amazon’s Biggest Business
items.summary: Amazon quietly became America's largest company by revenue, yet holiday shoppers and Wall Street investors seem far more focused on its AI ambitions than its massive e-commerce engine, and that split attention may be hiding a serious risk.

items.title: Target vs. Walmart: Holiday marketing’s stakes feel higher this year
items.summary: Walmart’s brand platform focused on reappraisal and Target’s turnaround strategy are in the spotlight during a make-or-break moment for retail.

items.title: Amazon’s Good Problems to Have Keep Me Hitting The Buy Button
items.summary: AWS capacity keeps selling out before Amazon can build it, retail margins hit record highs, and the capex bill is climbing toward $220 billion. Here is why those problems look like reasons to own more shares rather than reasons to worry.

items.title: Target Yields Nearly 4 Times Walmart. Which Dividend Is Better for Retirement?
items.summary: Both retailers raised guidance and collected tariff refunds, but how they pay shareholders could not be more different, and for retirees that gap matters more than any quarterly earnings beat.
